process_area.title: AI Strategy, Governance Framework & Model Risk Management

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Data & Analytics (links to VS-28/VS-30.2), Enterprise Architecture (links to VS-113), IT/Security (links to VS-27/VS-27.3), Privacy/DPO (links to VS-91), Legal (links to VS-100), Risk/Internal Audit (links to VS-21), HR (links to VS-19/VS-103), business AI owners (Fraud links to VS-125, CDP links to VS-126, S&OP links to VS-127, Marketing links to VS-14, LP links to VS-23)
fields.Trigger: Digital/data strategy (links to VS-28/VS-113); AI-program review

workflows.name: AI/ML Strategy, Operating Model & Governance Framework

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enterprise AI strategy and governance framework" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "count, value, incidents, fairness pass-rate" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve the AI budget" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-614 (ensure controlled execution — AI Strategy, Governance Framework & Model Risk Management (PA-128.1).); CTL-147 (ensure AI model risk & human-oversight control — cross-reference.)
- operational: central AI-governance framework; operational: ISO 42001/NIST AI RMF baseline
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-owner risk**: AI/ML proliferates with no governance owner; mitigated by central AI-governance framework
- **Framework-shopping risk**: Adopts no standard; mitigated by ISO 42001/NIST AI RMF baseline
System Touchpoints: - Data/analytics (links to VS-28); AI/ML platform (links to VS-30.2); EA (links to VS-113); security (links to VS-27.3); privacy (links to VS-91); risk/audit (links to VS-21); legal (links to VS-100)

steps.activity: AI Governance/CIO define the enterprise AI strategy and governance framework: the AI-use-case portfolio and roadmap, the governance operating model (AI steering, AI ethics review board, model-risk function), alignment to enterprise architecture (links to VS-113) and data strategy (links to VS-28), and the framework baseline (ISO 42001 AI Management System, NIST AI RMF)

AI Governance establish the governance scope and boundaries: which AI/ML is in scope (incl. vendor and GenAI), the risk-tiering approach, the interaction with privacy (links to VS-91), security (links to VS-27.3), audit (links to VS-21), and legal (links to VS-100), and the AI value/KPIs (model count, value, incidents, fairness pass-rate)
CIO/Executive ratify the strategy and governance, approve the AI budget (links to W3935), and cascade accountability to business AI owners

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Risk (links to VS-21), Legal (links to VS-100), Privacy (links to VS-91), Security (links to VS-27.3), HR (links to VS-19), business AI owners, Compliance (links to VS-22)
fields.Trigger: Strategy (W3929); new AI use-case; regulatory change

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "AI Governance/HR publish AI acceptable-use for employees" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-147 (ensure AI model risk & human-oversight control.)
- operational: acceptable-use policy and monitoring (links to VS-27); operational: annual + on-change refresh
Pain Points / Risks: - **Shadow-AI risk**: Employees use ungoverned GenAI/tools with confidential data; mitigated by acceptable-use policy and monitoring (links to VS-27.3)
- **Policy-staleness risk**: Policy lags AI/GenAI evolution and regulation; mitigated by annual + on-change refresh
System Touchpoints: - Policy/standards library; risk (links to VS-21); privacy (links to VS-91); security (links to VS-27.3); legal (links to VS-100); L&D (links to VS-19.4); compliance (links to VS-22)

steps.a: CIO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: AI Governance/Risk/Legal author the AI/ML policy and standards: acceptable/prohibited AI uses, data-use rules, fairness/non-discrimination, human-oversight requirements, explainability thresholds, GenAI acceptable-use, and risk appetite (tolerable bias, error, autonomy by tier)
AI Governance/HR publish AI acceptable-use for employees (GenAI tools, data-input rules, confidentiality, IP — links to VS-19.4 training), and enforce via access and monitoring (links to VS-27.3)

AI Governance/Compliance align policy to RA 10173 (automated decisions/profiling — links to VS-91), Consumer Act (links to VS-22), sector expectations, and monitor emerging PH AI regulation (links to W3944)

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), business AI owners (VS-125/VS-126/VS-127/VS-14/VS-23), IT (links to VS-27), Privacy (links to VS-91), Risk (links to VS-21)
fields.Volume: ~8–12 BuildRight-built production AI/ML models per the PA-30.2 canon (fraud, forecast, personalization, pricing, LP, chatbot, GenAI), plus vendor/embedded models outside this registry

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enterprise model inventory/registry" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconcile the registry to actual production models" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-147 (ensure AI model risk & human-oversight control.)
- operational: discovery and registry control; operational: consistent tiering criteria
Pain Points / Risks: - **Shadow-model risk**: Models in production not registered/governed; mitigated by discovery and registry control
- **Tier-misassignment risk**: High-risk model under-controlled; mitigated by consistent tiering criteria
System Touchpoints: - Model registry; ML platform (links to VS-30.2); IT ops (links to VS-27); privacy (links to VS-91); risk/audit (links to VS-21)

steps.activity: AI Governance maintain the enterprise model inventory/registry: model ID, owner, purpose, data sources, tier, deployment, dependencies, version, status, last validation, and link to the use-case owner (e.g., fraud model → VS-125, forecast → VS-127, recommendation → VS-126)

AI Governance/Risk tier each model by risk (high/medium/low) based on impact (revenue, customer-harm potential, rights-affecting, safety, scale), data sensitivity (PII links to VS-91), and autonomy — driving the depth of controls (links to W3932)

AI Governance reconcile the registry to actual production models (discover shadow models), retire decommissioned models (links to W3948), and report the inventory to the AI steering and audit (links to VS-21)

fields.Participants: Model Risk (independent — links to VS-21), AI Governance, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), business AI owners, Privacy (links to VS-91), Internal Audit (links to VS-21)
fields.Trigger: New/deployed model (links to W3931); validation cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document findings, and require remediation before approval" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track findings to closure, and report model risk to the AI steering and Audit…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-147 (ensure AI model risk & human-oversight control.)
- operational: independent validation (three lines of defense links to W3933); operational: closure tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Self-marking risk**: Model builder validates own model (conflict); mitigated by independent validation (three lines of defense links to W3933)
- **Findings-backlog risk**: Validation findings not remediated; mitigated by closure tracking
System Touchpoints: - Model registry (links to W3931); data quality (links to VS-28.2); ML platform (links to VS-30.2); risk register (links to VS-21); audit committee (links to VS-36)
Time Estimate: - ~1–3 weeks per tier-1 model validation + periodic revalidation

steps.activity: Model Risk/AI-Governance run model-risk assessment per model: data quality/lineage (links to VS-28.2), conceptual soundness, performance/accuracy, bias/fairness (links to W3937), explainability (links to W3938), privacy (links to W3939), and dependency/operational risk
Model Risk perform independent validation (challenge) of tier-1/2 models before deployment and on revalidation cycle, document findings, and require remediation before approval
AI Governance/Model-Risk maintain the model-risk register, track findings to closure, and report model risk to the AI steering and Audit Committee (links to VS-21/VS-36)

fields.Participants: AI Governance, CIO, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), business AI owners, Model Risk (links to VS-21), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), IT/Security (links to VS-27), Privacy (links to VS-91), HR (links to VS-19)

workflows.name: AI/ML Roles, Ownership & the Three Lines of Defense

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accountable for outcome" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "AI Governance operate the three lines of defense" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-create of "create unacceptable conflicts of interest" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-614 (ensure controlled execution — AI Strategy, Governance Framework & Model Risk Management (PA-128.1).)
- operational: explicit RACI and three-lines model; operational: competency/talent plan (links to VS-19)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Role-confusion risk**: Unclear who owns model risk; mitigated by explicit RACI and three-lines model
- **Skills-gap risk**: Insufficient model-risk/validation talent; mitigated by competency/talent plan (links to VS-19.4)
System Touchpoints: - RACI/roles; model risk (links to VS-21); audit (links to VS-21); L&D (links to VS-19.4); HR (links to VS-19)

steps.activity: AI Governance define AI/ML roles and RACI: business use-case owner (accountable for outcome), data-science builder (links to VS-30.2), model-risk validator (independent — 2nd line links to VS-21), internal audit (3rd line links to VS-21), and the AI governance function (oversight)

steps.a: CIO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: AI Governance operate the three lines of defense: 1st line (build/operate/monitor), 2nd line (model risk/policy challenge), 3rd line (independent audit), with clear separation between model builder and validator
AI Governance/HR define AI-competency/talent needs (links to VS-19.4/VS-123), and ensure role assignments don't create unacceptable conflicts of interest

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Procurement (links to VS-34), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Security (links to VS-27.3), Privacy (links to VS-91), IT/EA (links to VS-27/VS-113), Data Science (links to VS-30.2), ABC (links to VS-86.3)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "AI Governance/Procurement/Legal assess and contract AI vendors, open-source models" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor vendor AI performance/SLA" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-147 (ensure AI model risk & human-oversight control.)
- operational: DPIA and contract terms (links to VS-91); operational: provenance review and monitoring
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-egress risk**: PII/confidential data sent to vendor/foundation models without basis; mitigated by DPIA and contract terms (links to VS-91)
- **Model-poisoning risk**: Open-source/foundation models compromised; mitigated by provenance review and monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/contracts (links to VS-34/VS-100.3); security (links to VS-27.3); privacy (links to VS-91); EA (links to VS-113); ABC (links to VS-86.3); vendor SLA (links to VS-27 W369)

steps.activity: AI Governance/Procurement/Legal assess and contract AI vendors, open-source models, and foundation-model/LLM providers: data-processing terms (RA 10173 links to VS-91), IP/output ownership, model-card/transparency, security review (links to VS-27.3), and ABC-compliant sourcing (links to VS-86.3)

AI Governance/Security govern vendor AI risk: data egress (customer/PII to vendor models), model provenance/poisoning for open-source, vendor model-change/refresh impact, and concentration risk on a single foundation model
AI Governance/IT monitor vendor AI performance/SLA (links to VS-27 W369), manage vendor-model retirement/migration, and maintain the vendor-AI register feeding the model inventory (links to W3931)

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Finance (links to VS-17.4), Data & Analytics (links to VS-28/VS-30.2), IT/FinOps (links to VS-27.2), HR (links to VS-19.4/VS-123), EA (links to VS-113), business AI owners
fields.Trigger: Annual budget (links to VS-33.1); platform/talent cycle
fields.Volume: AI program budget, platform, and talent plan

Automation Opportunity: - workflow automation; system-driven processing with exception handling
Controls: - CTL-614 (ensure controlled execution — AI Strategy, Governance Framework & Model Risk Management (PA-128.1).)
- operational: FinOps (links to VS-27); operational: talent plan and partnerships
Pain Points / Risks: - **Compute-cost risk**: AI/GenAI compute cost spirals uncontrolled; mitigated by FinOps (links to VS-27.2)
- **Talent-shortage risk**: Scarce AI/model-risk talent; mitigated by talent plan and partnerships
System Touchpoints: - Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4); ML platform (links to VS-30.2); FinOps (links to VS-27.2); EA (links to VS-113); L&D/talent (links to VS-19.4/VS-123); privacy (links to VS-91)

steps.activity: AI Governance/Finance develop the AI budget (platform/compute, talent, vendor models, governance), align to annual budget (links to VS-33.1/VS-17.4), and size value vs cost (links to W3951)

AI Governance/IT/EA manage the AI/ML platform and compute (links to VS-30.2/VS-27.2 FinOps W373), environment/data-privacy segregation (links to VS-91), and MLOps tooling aligned to architecture (links to VS-113)
AI Governance/HR build the AI-talent plan (data science, ML engineering, model risk, AI governance — links to VS-19.4/VS-123), and address skills gaps via hiring/training

fields.Participants: AI Governance, CIO, Strategy (links to VS-33), Risk/Internal Audit (links to VS-21), Data & Analytics (links to VS-28), business AI owners, Innovation (links to VS-30)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "AI Governance/CIO run the annual AI-maturity assessment" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "AI Governance develop the maturity-improvement roadmap" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track maturity progression, and report to the executive committee and Audit…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-614 (ensure controlled execution — AI Strategy, Governance Framework & Model Risk Management (PA-128.1).)
- operational: annual assessment and exec sponsorship; operational: balanced roadmap
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stalled-maturity risk**: Governance maturity stalls without progression; mitigated by annual assessment and exec sponsorship
- **Tooling-over-governance risk**: Investing in AI platform without governance depth; mitigated by balanced roadmap
System Touchpoints: - Maturity model; strategy (links to VS-33); risk/audit (links to VS-21); data/analytics (links to VS-28); innovation (links to VS-30); audit committee (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: AI Governance/CIO run the annual AI-maturity assessment (strategy, governance, data, platform, talent, responsible-AI, value — vs ISO 42001/NIST AI RMF maturity), benchmark vs retail peers, and identify gaps

AI Governance develop the maturity-improvement roadmap (governance depth links to W3930, model-risk links to W3932, responsible-AI links to W3937–W3944, monitoring links to W3947), prioritized with executive sponsorship
AI Governance execute quarterly improvement actions, track maturity progression, and report to the executive committee and Audit Committee (links to VS-33/VS-36)
